ar.q1: What is augmented reality (AR) and how is it used here?
ar.a1: Augmented reality is a technology that allows digital elements —such as characters, objects or scenes— to be overlaid onto the real environment through your mobile phone’s camera. In this game, it is used to see Miula, deactivate explosive artefacts and view collectibles.
ar.q2: Can I take photos or videos with AR?
ar.a2: Yes! You can take photos (screenshots) and record videos with Miula and the different AR experiences, and share them. It’s a great way to remember and share your adventure.
ar.q3: Do I need to download an app?
ar.a3: No. This is a web application (webapp): you only need to access the link using your browser (Chrome, Safari, etc.). No download is required.
ar.q4: Is my phone compatible with augmented reality?
ar.a4: It works on most recent devices with a camera and an up-to-date browser. You must grant permission to access the camera. If you experience issues, try another browser or device.
ar.q5: I don’t see anything when I open the camera. What can I do?
ar.a5: Make sure that:​ ● You have physically arrived at the correct point on the map (geolocation).​ ● You have granted camera access permission.​ ● There is enough light in the environment.​ If it still doesn’t work, close and reopen the browser.
ar.q6: Do I need an internet connection to use AR?
ar.a6: Yes. Augmented reality loads in the browser, so you need a mobile data or Wi-Fi connection during the experience.
ar.q7: Is it safe to use augmented reality while walking?
ar.a7: Yes, but you must stay aware of your physical surroundings while using the camera. Do not walk while staring at your phone and always pay attention to your environment.

game.q1: What is the objective of the game?
game.a1: The goal is to accompany Miula across thirteen geolocated points, where she will explain stories related to each location. You will need to deactivate explosive artefacts, answer questions and collect collectibles.
game.q2: How do I deactivate explosive artefacts and obtain collectibles?
game.a2: You must physically reach the geolocated points shown on the map. There, Miula will tell a story and propose an interactive challenge and a question. If you complete them successfully, you will obtain a collectible related to that point.
game.q3: What happens if I fail a challenge or a question?
game.a3: Interactive challenges are completed by deactivating a specific number of explosive artefacts using AR. The challenge will not end until all artefacts are deactivated. Usually there are between six and seven. If a question is answered incorrectly, the system asks you to try again.
game.q4: Do I need to register to play?
game.a4: Yes, registration is mandatory to participate in the game, access augmented reality points and unlock Roman coins and different collectibles. This allows us to save your progress, offer a personalised experience and ensure proper system operation. Registration is quick and only needs to be done once.
game.q5: Can I play in a group or with my family?
game.a5: Yes! The game is designed to be played in groups: with friends, family or school groups. You only need one mobile phone or tablet per team and a desire to explore the territory together.

map.q1: How does the game map work?
map.a1: The interactive map shows the geolocated points that make up the route. Augmented reality content is only unlocked when you physically arrive at a point.
map.q2: Do I need to enable geolocation on my phone?
map.a2: Yes. Without geolocation enabled, the game cannot be played. The system needs to know your location to verify that you have correctly moved to each point. We recommend enabling location services before starting the route. How to enable geolocation on your device: On an Android phone 1.​ Open Settings.​ 2.​ Go to Location.​ 3.​ Enable Location.​ 4.​ Make sure your browser (Chrome, Firefox, etc.) has permission:​ – Settings > Apps > [Browser name] > Permissions > Location > Allow always or While using the app.​ On an iPhone 1.​ Open Settings.​ 2.​ Go to Privacy & Security > Location Services.​ 3.​ Enable Location Services.​ 4.​ Open the browser settings (usually Safari or Chrome).​ 5.​ Check that Location is set to While Using the App.​
map.q3: What should I do if the map doesn’t detect my location correctly?
map.a3: ● Check that location services are enabled.​ ● Reload the browser page.
map.q4: Do I need an internet connection to use the map?
map.a4: Yes. The webapp requires an active connection to display the map and validate your position. However, data usage is very low.
map.q5: The map says I’m not in the right place, but I know I am. What should I do?
map.a5: ● Move slightly around the area: GPS signals sometimes take a few seconds to update.​ ● Make sure you are not under a structure or inside an enclosed space.​ ● Ensure you have good GPS or mobile network coverage.
map.q6: Can I do the route in any order?
map.a6: No. The route is linear. You must follow the established order of the points, as each challenge and discovery depends on the previous one. The map will only show the next unlocked point, and you cannot advance without completing the current one.

Caminslogin.text: Hello! I’m Miula, the owl of memory, and I will be your guide. For a long time, I have been flying over towns, paths and landscapes, keeping the stories hidden within our territory. The Paths of Memory invite you to explore real places in order to better understand our recent past. Each path brings us closer to moments, places and experiences that have left their mark, even if they are not always visible at first glance. Through these routes, you will discover how history shaped the everyday lives of many people: what was built, what was defended, but also what was suffered, what had to adapt and, often, what had to be lived in silence.You will not only listen to stories: you will take part in them. Along the paths, I will propose interactive challenges using augmented reality, as well as questions that will help you observe each place more carefully and understand what happened there. As you progress, you will be able to collect digital items linked to the places you discover. Each route focuses on a different aspect of democratic memory, but they all share the same approach: walking, observing, playing and reflecting. It is not just about reaching a place, but about experiencing it and understanding why it is part of our collective memory. If you join me, I will guide you along the different paths, explain what happened in each location and help you discover how the past still dialogues with the present. Whenever you’re ready, you can choose which path you want to start with. See you soon!

Rutaintro.text: I’m Miula, the owl of memory, and for a long time I have been flying over our coastline, keeping the stories hidden within it. Many years ago, during the Spanish Civil War, along the coast of Sitges, Vilanova i la Geltrú, Cubelles, Cunit, Calafell and El Vendrell, bunkers, trenches and fortifications were built to protect the towns from a possible attack from the sea. Today, these places help us understand history and what everyday life was like at that time, shaped by fear, waiting, collective organisation and the silences that many people had to keep in order to survive. If you join me, I will tell you the stories of each place and help you discover why they are so important to our collective memory. Your mission will be to help me deactivate old explosive devices using augmented reality. Once you succeed, I will ask you a question to check whether you have been paying attention to my explanations.​ If you answer correctly, you will receive a 3D collectible object related to the place you have just discovered. Are you ready?​ I’ll be waiting for you at the different points along the route. See you soon!

Rutaend.text: You have reached the end of the path. Throughout this route, you have explored real places that, during a difficult period, were part of the everyday lives of many people. Places of surveillance, organisation and waiting, built with the intention of protecting, but also marked by fear and uncertainty. Each bunker, each trench and each fortification holds stories that could not always be told out loud. Stories of neighbours, soldiers and entire families who learned to live with silence, with constant alertness and with the hope that the conflict would come to an end. Today, thanks to your curiosity and your way of looking, these places speak again. Not as elements of war, but as witnesses of the past that help us better understand the present. Remembering is not about looking back with nostalgia, but about becoming aware of what happened so it is not repeated. Democratic memory is built this way: by walking, listening and sharing. Thank you for helping me preserve these stories and for being part of this memory route. I will continue flying over the coast, keeping these stories and waiting for more people, like you, to want to listen to them. Until the next route.

Description.text3: Along the coastline of the Garraf and the Baix Penedès there are places that tell an important part of our recent history. Bunkers, forts and other defensive structures are still preserved along the coast, although they often go unnoticed. This route invites you to discover these sites and to understand why they were built during the Spanish Civil War. Through different points located in Sitges, Vilanova i la Geltrú, Cubelles, Cunit, Calafell and El Vendrell, you will learn how towns were defended, what daily life was like at that time, and what these places tell us today. The points are spread across several municipalities, so it is recommended to complete the route in stages, at your own pace, starting wherever you wish. With the help of Miula, you will observe, listen and interact with each site to understand why these places form part of our collective memory.
Description.text7: Sitges, Vilanova i la Geltrú, Cubelles, Cunit, Calafell and El Vendrell
Description.text9: Most of the points on the route are accessible via paths, seafront promenades or urban areas, and all of them can be reached without special difficulty. One point on the route (Punta Mabrera Bunker, in Vilanova i la Geltrú) is located in a rocky coastal area with more irregular access. In this case, access may be more difficult for people with reduced mobility or for those using pushchairs.
Description.text11: This experience is designed to be shared with family or in groups, with children aged 8 and over, young people and adults, allowing the content, explanations and challenges to be discussed and reflected upon together. The route can be completed calmly and at your own pace. It is not necessary to visit all points in a single day, as the sites are spread along the coastline and each stop works as an independent discovery.Some points are outdoors, close to the sea. Comfortable footwear, sun protection and water are recommended, especially during warmer months. The sites along the route form part of the landscape and cultural heritage. We ask that you observe them with respect and leave no litter behind. When completing the route with children, adult supervision is recommended, especially in areas close to the coast.

To ensure the activation of game points and personalize the experience.
To maintain security and improve the services offered.
To communicate news or information related to the application, with the user's prior consent.
